label.text: 7 DRUG INTERACTIONS Cyclosporine: Avoid simultaneous coadministration with XENICAL. Administer cyclosporine 3 hours after XENICAL. Monitor for eﬀectiveness. ( 7 ) Fat-soluble Vitamin Supplements and Analogues: Administer a multivitamin supplement at least 2 hours before or 2 hours after the administration of XENICAL, or at bedtime. ( 7 ) Levothyroxine: Avoid simultaneous coadministration with XENICAL. Administer levothyroxine and XENICAL at least 4 hours apart. Monitor for changes in thyroid function. ( 7 ) Anticoagulants including Warfarin: Monitor for changes in coagulation parameters. ( 7 ) Amiodarone: Monitor patients as clinically indicated. ( 7 ) Antiepileptic Drugs: Monitor patients for changes in seizure frequency. ( 7 ) Antiretroviral Drugs: Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently and discontinue XENICAL if there is an increase in HIV viral load. ( 7 ) Table 4 describes the clinically signiﬁcant drug and dietary supplement interactions with XENICAL. Table 4 Clinically Signiﬁcant Drug and Dietary Supplement Interactions with XENICAL Cyclosporine Clinical Impact Coadministration of XENICAL and cyclosporine reduces cyclosporine plasma levels [see Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.3 )]. Intervention Avoid simultaneous coadministration of XENICAL and cyclosporine. Administer cyclosporine 3 hours after the administration of XENICAL. In those patients whose cyclosporine levels are being measured, monitor more frequently [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.1 )] . Fat-soluble Vitamin Supplements and Analogues Clinical Impact The absorption of beta-carotene supplements is reduced when concomitantly administered with XENICAL. XENICAL also inhibited absorption of a vitamin E acetate supplement. The eﬀect of XENICAL on the absorption of supplemental vitamin D, vitamin A, and nutritionally-derived vitamin K is not known [see Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.3 ) and Warnings and Precautions ( 5.1 )]. Intervention Administer a multivitamin supplement at least 2 hours before or 2 hours after the administration of XENICAL, or at bedtime [see Dosage and Administration ( 2 )] . Levothyroxine Clinical Impact Hypothyroidism has been reported in patients treated concomitantly with XENICAL and levothyroxine postmarketing. Intervention Avoid simultaneous coadministration of XENICAL and levothyroxine. Administer levothyroxine and XENICAL at least 4 hours apart [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.1 ) and Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.3 )] . Monitor patients treated concomitantly with XENICAL and levothyroxine for changes in thyroid function. Anticoagulants including Warfarin Clinical Impact Vitamin K absorption may be decreased with XENICAL. Reports of decreased prothrombin, increased INR and unbalanced anticoagulant treatment resulting in change of hemostatic parameters have been reported in patients treated concomitantly with XENICAL and anticoagulants. Intervention Monitor patients on warfarin or other anticoagulants who are prescribed XENICAL for changes in coagulation parameters [see Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.3 )] . Amiodarone Clinical Impact Coadministration of XENICAL and amiodarone reduces exposure to amiodarone and its metabolite, desethylamiodarone [see Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.3 )] . A reduced therapeutic eﬀect of amiodarone is possible. The eﬀect of commencing orlistat treatment in patients on stable amiodarone therapy has not been studied. Intervention Monitor patients as clinically indicated. Antiepileptic Drugs Clinical Impact XENICAL may decrease the eﬀect of antiepileptic drugs. Convulsions have been reported in patients treated concomitantly with orlistat and antiepileptic drugs. Intervention Monitor patients for changes in seizure frequency. Antiretroviral Drugs Clinical Impact Loss of virological control has been reported in HIV-infected patients taking orlistat concomitantly with antiretroviral drugs such as atazanavir, ritonavir, tenofovir disoproxil fumarate, emtricitabine, and with the combinations lopinavir/ritonavir and emtricitabine/efavirenz/tenofovir disoproxil fumarate. The exact mechanism for this is unclear, but may include a drug-drug interaction that inhibits systemic absorption of the antiretroviral drug. Intervention HIV RNA levels should be frequently monitored in patients who take XENICAL while being treated for HIV infection. Discontinue XENICAL if there is a conﬁrmed increase in HIV viral load.

sections.contraindications: 4 CONTRAINDICATIONS XENICAL is contraindicated in patients with: chronic malabsorption syndrome [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.1 )] cholestasis known hypersensitivity to orlistat or any of the inactive ingredients in XENICAL. Serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylactic reactions and angioedema, have been reported with XENICAL [see Adverse Reactions ( 6.2 )]. Chronic malabsorption syndrome ( 4 ) Cholestasis ( 4 ) Known hypersensitivity to orlistat or any of the inactive ingredients in XENICAL ( 4 )
sections.pregnancy:
8.1 Pregnancy Risk Summary Available data from published prospective and retrospective cohort studies over decades of use with XENICAL during pregnancy have not identiﬁed an increased risk of major birth defects, miscarriage or other adverse maternal or fetal outcomes. However, weight loss oﬀers no beneﬁt to a pregnant patient and may result in a small for gestational age infant. When a pregnancy is recognized, advise the pregnant patient of the risk to a fetus and discontinue XENICAL ( see Clinical Considerations ). Oral administration of orlistat to pregnant rats and rabbits during the period of organogenesis did not show any adverse embryofetal eﬀects at doses 23 times and 47 times, respectively, the maximum recommended human dose (MRHD) based on body surface area (mg/m 2 ) ( see Data ). The background risk of major birth defects and miscarriage for the indicated population is unknown. All pregnancies have a background risk of birth defect, loss, or other adverse outcomes. In the U.S. general population, the estimated background risk of major birth defects and miscarriage in clinically recognized pregnancies is 2 to 4% and 15 to 20%, respectively. Clinical Considerations Disease-associated maternal and/or embryo/fetal risk Appropriate weight gain based on pre-pregnancy weight is currently recommended for all pregnant patients, including those who have overweight or obesity, because of the obligatory weight gain that occurs in maternal tissues during pregnancy. Data Animal Data In embryofetal development studies in pregnant rats and rabbits administered orlistat during organogenesis, no adverse embryofetal eﬀects were seen at doses up to 800 mg/kg/day, corresponding to 23 times and 47 times MRHD, respectively based on body surface area (mg/m 2 ). In a pre- and post-natal development study in pregnant rats dosed orlistat during gestation through lactation, no adverse developmental eﬀects were observed in the oﬀspring at doses up to 400 mg/kg/day, corresponding to 12 times MRHD, based on body surface area (mg/m 2 ).

sections.information_for_patients: 17 PATIENT COUNSELING INFORMATION Advise the patient to read the FDA-approved patient labeling (Patient Information). Loss of Eﬀect of Certain Medications and Dietary Supplements with Coadministration of XENICAL Advise patients taking cyclosporine, levothyroxine, warfarin, amiodarone, antiepileptic drugs, antiretroviral drugs, certain fat-soluble vitamins, and beta carotene that XENICAL may reduce their eﬀectiveness [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.1 ) and Drug Interactions ( 7 )] . Liver Injury Inform patients of the risk of liver injury and educate patients on the signs and symptoms of hepatic dysfunction (anorexia, pruritus, jaundice, dark urine, light-colored stools, or right upper quadrant pain). Instruct patients to contact their health care provider if they experience signs or symptoms of hepatic dysfunction [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.2 )]. Oxalate Nephrolithiasis and Oxalate Nephropathy with Renal Failure Inform patients of the potential risk for oxalate nephrolithiasis and oxalate nephropathy and explain the associated signs and symptoms, including of renal failure. Instruct patients to contact their health care provider if they experience signs or symptoms of oxalate nephrolithiasis or oxalate nephropathy [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.3 )]. Acute Gallbladder Disease Inform patients of the risk of acute gallbladder disease. Instruct patients to contact their health care provider for appropriate clinical follow-up if gallbladder disease is suspected [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.4 )]. Gastrointestinal Events Inform patients of the risk of the commonly-observed gastrointestinal adverse events associated with the use of XENICAL which include oily spotting, ﬂatus with discharge, fecal urgency, fatty/oily stool, oily evacuation, increased defecation, and fecal incontinence. Advise patients to adhere to dietary guidelines to distribute the daily intake of fat over three main meals [see Dosage and Administration ( 2 )] . Advise patients that if XENICAL is taken with any one meal very high in fat, the possibility of gastrointestinal eﬀects increases [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.5 )] .
